answers.answer: No. Reserved cards have not been purchased, so their printed prestige does not count toward your score or the 15-point trigger, and their bonuses do not reduce costs or satisfy nobles.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources: "Development cards | Printed on each purchased card"; payment uses "previously purchased development cards"; nobles require "bonuses (from purchased development cards)."

answers.answer: You receive no physical blue token. The purchased card permanently adds one blue bonus for future purchases, and that bonus can help satisfy a noble even though the card has zero prestige.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: "Each purchased development card adds exactly one bonus of its color permanently" and "Bonuses reduce costs but never generate tokens." Components says prestige "may be 0"; nobles require bonuses from purchased cards.

answers.answer: Its own bonus cannot make the purchase free: payment discounts come from previously purchased cards, so you cannot afford it with no blue bonus, blue token, or gold. A newly purchased white-bonus card does count toward the noble checked at the end of this turn.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: "Each bonus from previously purchased development cards" reduces payment. Turn Structure checks for a noble "After performing their action"; qualification uses bonuses "from purchased development cards."

answers.answer: The excess blue bonuses cannot pay green costs and do not produce blue tokens as change. The blue cost is covered; you still need two green tokens, or gold substituted for some or all of those two tokens.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: excess bonuses in "a particular color" provide "no benefit for that purchase (no change is given)." Gold can "substitute for any single gem token."

answers.answer: The bonuses remain; they are permanent, not spent on the first noble. If the other noble remains available, taking gems on your next turn can still be followed by receiving it at the end of that turn. You cannot receive it during an opponent’s intervening turn.
answers.evidence: Bonuses are permanent. Noble Visits: "At the end of their turn, a player checks" qualification; when multiple qualify, "choose one" and "The other noble(s) remain available for future turns."

answers.answer: Yes. You may reserve that level-3 card despite being unable to buy it. Reserving takes a card into your hand without paying its printed purchase cost, and gives you one gold token if available.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card permits "A face-up development card from the 3x4 grid" and says "Upon reserving, also take 1 gold token." Printed payment belongs to the separate purchase action; the reservation limit is at most three cards.

answers.answer: No market card is removed or refilled: you take the top card directly from the level-2 deck, leaving all twelve face-up market cards. You take only that one card into your hand, with no second replacement card.
answers.evidence: Reservation takes "one development card," including "The top card from any one of the three level decks." Replacement applies "When a face-up card is purchased (or reserved) from the grid."

answers.answer: The four face-up cards remain available to purchase or reserve. Buying one leaves its space empty because its deck is empty; the other three remain in the market.
answers.evidence: Purchase permits a face-up card from the grid; reservation permits a face-up card. Card Replacement: "If the corresponding deck is empty, the empty space in the grid remains empty for the rest of the game."

answers.answer: The summary gives reaching 15 prestige as its end-game trigger, but does not explicitly address whether complete card exhaustion itself ends the game; that specific exhaustion ruling is unsupported. If play continues, its action rules permit buying the affordable reserved card or taking one gem from each of three available colors.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: "When any player reaches 15 or more prestige points, the current round is completed." Purchase allows "a previously reserved card from your hand"; the different-color action takes one from each of three color piles. No full-market-exhaustion ending rule is stated.

answers.answer: Yes. You may take the three tokens, temporarily reach thirteen, then return all three just taken and finish with your original ten. No net token gain is required by these rules.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "A player may temporarily exceed 10 during their action" and "may return some or all of the tokens they just took."

answers.answer: A’s two spent gold tokens return to the supply. B can take one when reserving, leaving one gold token in the supply immediately afterward, before any token-limit returns.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: "Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply." Reserving takes "1 gold token" if available.

answers.answer: Yes. The purchase action allows a face-up development from the grid when you can pay its cost; it gives no prerequisite to buy lower-level cards first.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card: "Purchase a face-up development card from the grid or a previously reserved card from your hand by paying the gem token cost shown on the card."

answers.answer: You cannot skip the qualifying noble: the visit is automatic and cannot be refused. You finish the turn at eighteen prestige (12 + 3 + 3). Players who still have turns in the current round continue so everyone has taken the same number of turns.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "A noble visit is automatic -- a player cannot refuse it" and each noble is worth "3 prestige points." End-Game Trigger completes the current round so all have "the same number of turns."

answers.answer: The game ends after D completes that turn. A, B, C, and D have then taken equal numbers of turns, so the current round is already complete; A does not begin another round and nobody receives an extra turn.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: "the current round is completed so that every player has played the same number of turns."

answers.answer: No new noble is revealed from the removed seven. The acquired tile goes face-up in front of the receiving player, leaving two nobles available in the middle.
answers.evidence: Setup: "Remove remaining noble tiles from the game -- they will not be used." Noble Visits: "Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you." Noble Tile Mechanics says removed tiles are "out of the game permanently."

answers.answer: Emerald is green; diamond is white; sapphire is blue; onyx is black; ruby is red; gold joker is yellow. There are ninety development cards: forty level 1, thirty level 2, and twenty level 3.
answers.evidence: Components token table lists Emerald/Green, Diamond/White, Sapphire/Blue, Onyx/Black, Ruby/Red, Gold (Joker)/Yellow. Development Cards lists "90 total": Level 1 40, Level 2 30, Level 3 20.
